- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of history.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per event to reflect volatility dampening.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish spikes followed by bearish corrections, model fails to anticipate reversal; apply lagged correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast 3–5 days after peak.
